# Backspace Fork 1.15.6

## Changes

- **Optional H.265 / HEVC screen sharing:** Added an H265 (HEVC) choice when the Chromium/WebRTC sender advertises support. VP9 remains the default and cameras remain H.264. Devices without HEVC publishing support keep the saved preference but use H.264 locally.
- **Single-codec compatibility fallback:** HEVC requests use LiveKit's codec-regression policy with a full-quality H.264 fallback for incompatible viewers, rather than permanent parallel encoders. Changing between HEVC and explicit H.264 updates the backup policy even when both use H.264 locally.
- **Voice priority and stream controls:** Video yields to microphone traffic, sender-wide priority is applied to the first encoding, and quality ceilings target the highest layer. HEVC fallback senders and later-created fallback encodings follow live bitrate/FPS changes. Existing capture, system audio and republish/reconnect behavior is preserved.
- **Stream diagnostics and translations:** Diagnostics recognize HEVC and active cloned fallback senders instead of paused primaries. Late results from an old publication cannot overwrite the current codec. New capability/fallback help is translated into all five supported languages.
- **Rich presence for games and media:** Includes the previously merged game/launcher detection, game icons, media activity and profile activity improvements, along with federation/IPC validation and desktop reliability fixes.
- **Maintenance:** Includes Windows desktop test fixes and the updated security-scan baseline for resolved deepmerge findings.

## Compatibility and operations

- Chromium chooses the actual encoder; H.265 selection does not guarantee AMF, NVENC or hardware acceleration. Device, browser, driver and viewer compatibility still matter. A codec transition can briefly interrupt video, and automatic return to HEVC after an incompatible viewer leaves is not guaranteed.
- Actual HEVC RTP encode/decode, hardware performance and mixed-viewer fallback require validation on the target devices and SFU. Automated tests cover configuration and lifecycle behavior, not those hardware outcomes.
- This release includes the additive game-icons database migration already merged into master. Back up the database before updating; existing users, uploads and instance identity must be preserved. No minimum desktop version increase is required by this release.
